title: Constructibility for continuous coefficient module sheaves
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $A$ be a commutative topological ring. Write $A_X(V)=C(|V|,A)$, with pointwise operations and precomposition restrictions, for the continuous coefficient sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-lattice-sheaf-locally-constant]. The constant-section map from the constant ring sheaf, formed by sheafification [def-weil-pbc-adic-lisse-module], to $A_X$ sends $a$ to the constant function $a$. For an ordinary $A$-module $P$, define $A_X\otimes_A P$ by extension of scalars of its constant module sheaf along that map, using the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$, precomposition along $V\times_Y X\to V$ defines $A_Y\to f_*A_X$: these section maps commute with every restriction. Let $f^{-1}A_Y\to A_X$ be its adjoint under the pro-etale inverse/direct-image adjunction [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], and define the ringed inverse image $f^*N=A_X\otimes_{f^{-1}A_Y}f^{-1}N$. Now assume that the underlying topological space of $X$ is noetherian, meaning every descending chain of closed subsets stabilizes, as in Definition 6.8.10. An $A_X$-module sheaf $N$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is continuous-constructible if there is a finite locally closed stratification $X=\coprod S_i$ [def-constructible-stratification] such that, for each stratum inclusion $j_i:S_i\to X$, there is a pro-etale covering family $(V_a\to S_i)_a$ and, for every $a$, a finitely presented $A$-module $P_a$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] with $(j_i^*N)|_{V_a}\cong(A_{S_i}\otimes_A P_a)|_{V_a}$. Both the covering family and the finitely presented modules may vary with the stratum.

lean.note: Canonical coefficient maps, ordinary constant-module scalar extension, and ringed pullback are constructed, not chosen. The named naturality theorem postpones only the proof of the restriction law explicitly included in this definition node. Maintainer correction: constructibility is defined on topologically noetherian schemes, exactly as in Definition 6.8.10. This makes the inherited constructibility condition on stratification parts automatic; all coefficient and pullback constructions remain general.
